subject.title: [Feature]: Reusable gateway WebSocket client SDK package

question: Should OpenClaw publish a supported raw Gateway WebSocket client package now, and if so what package/API/security boundary should it commit to?
rationale: The remaining work is not a mechanical extraction: it defines a public auth, storage, transport, versioning, and adapter contract for external clients.

options.title: Sponsor public SDK contract
options.body: Define the package name, supported Node/browser/mobile adapters, auth and token-storage responsibilities, docs, smoke proof, and compatibility policy before implementation.

options.title: Defer to protocol docs
options.body: Keep the package private for now and continue directing external clients to Gateway protocol/RPC plus reference implementations until the security and support bar is ready.

options.title: Fold into app-SDK trackers
options.body: Make the app-SDK happy-path and docs-boundary trackers canonical only if maintainers decide there should not be a separate raw Gateway client package.

recommendation.title: Sponsor public SDK contract
recommendation.body: Define the package name, supported Node/browser/mobile adapters, auth and token-storage responsibilities, docs, smoke proof, and compatibility policy before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the internal package extraction and related SDK package work, making him the best available owner for the publication/API-boundary decision.
